name: Reims

art.title: Szeptycki's Lancers Taking Prussians at Reims

summary: Napoleon fell on Saint-Priest's Russian and Prussian corps, which had taken Reims; Saint-Priest, an émigré Frenchman in Russian service, was mortally wounded, and the city was retaken.

forces.name: Ricard's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's leading infantry, which crossed the ravine of La Muire and took the heights of Sainte-Geneviève before the town; Pelleport's brigade overwhelmed the Prussian Landwehr in the cemetery at Ormes. Its attack on the Soissons gate failed until the Guard's guns blew it in.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
On Nafziger's return of 17 March the division had 940 men, in Pelleport's and Clavel's brigades; its battalions here are those of 12 March.
After Athies the division had about 650 men in seven battalions, fifty to a hundred and sixty each. They are shown at full size; the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Nafziger gives the battalions without brigades; they are split here, light and line, as the list takes them.
A brigade of four light battalions, where the list takes three regiments and one light regiment in the division, shows as a historical departure.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Lagrange's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's other division, which followed Ricard's on the road from Berry-au-Bac and joined the attack on the town.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
On Nafziger's return of 17 March the division had 2,060 men, in Joubert's and Fournier's brigades; its battalions here are those of 12 March, as its brigades are of February.
Its marine regiments were sailors and naval gunners of the fleet's artillery, brought inland in 1813; they fought well, and are shown as Line, the list's Veteran upgrade would suit them.

Nafziger gives the division as one brigade; its regiments are brigaded here as at La Rothière, after Nafziger's history as Wikipedia's order of battle has it. Battalion numbers he leaves out, and the division's artillery, are from his returns of 25 January and La Rothière.
Nafziger gives the 37th Line, but it is the 37th Léger, which served in the division at Leipzig; the 37th Line was in Duhesme's division of Victor's corps.
After Athies the division had about 1,400 men in twenty-one battalions; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.

Nafziger gives Marmont's artillery on this return only as a foot and a horse company of January; the batteries here are those of the 25 January return. Clavel's four regiments, where the list's brigade takes three, show as a historical departure.

forces.name: Arrighi's Division
forces.summary: Arrighi's depot battalions from Paris, which marched on Reims with Marmont's corps.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
On Nafziger's return of 17 March the infantry had 2,080 men, in Lucotte's brigade and another; its battalions here are those of 12 March.

On 12 March the division had about 1,800 men in twelve battalions. Nafziger gives them without brigades; they are split between two here, in his order, the first under Lucotte as on his return of 17 March. The provisional cavalry Nafziger gives Arrighi at Laon is with Bordesoulle's here.
Brigades of four regiments, where the list's take three, show as historical departures.

forces.name: Bordesoulle's Cavalry
forces.summary: The cavalry of Marmont's column, which caught the Prussian horse at Rosnay on the way to Reims; Merlin's division led the thrust towards Bezannes as the infantry attacked the town.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
Merlin's light division is the first two brigades, Bordesoulle's own heavy division Thiry's and Laville's.

Each brigade was made up of squadrons from the depots of many regiments: Nafziger names their parent regiments but not their strengths. They are grouped here as one unit for each kind of horse in a brigade, or two where a brigade had many, as they were formed into provisional regiments.
On 17 March each of these detachments had fifty to a hundred and twenty men, about 2,400 in all; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them all.
Two heavy cavalry brigades, where the list takes one, and cuirassiers and dragoons in one brigade show as historical departures.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.

forces.name: Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur
forces.formation: Cavalry Division, attached to the Guard
forces.summary: The Gardes d'Honneur, which led the assault on the town with Ricard's division; Piquet's brigade cut down the Prussians at Ormes, and Ségur's, with the 3rd Gardes d'Honneur, was trapped in the streets and largely destroyed.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
The Gardes d'Honneur, raised in 1813 from young men of means who equipped themselves and rode dressed as hussars, are the list's Hussars.
The division had only 896 men in five regiments; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit them.

Nafziger gives the division without brigades. Piquet's brigade of the 10th Hussars and the 1st Gardes d'Honneur, and Ségur's of the 3rd and 4th, are as at La Rothière; the 2nd Gardes d'Honneur are with Ségur's here, three hussar regiments where the list's brigade takes two, a historical departure.
A cavalry force on its own has no infantry brigade, which the list needs to allow its cavalry, so this shows as a historical departure. Play it alongside infantry, or agree it with your opponent.

forces.name: Colbert's Guard Cavalry
forces.summary: The Guard horse under Sébastiani, which advanced on Ricard's flanks as the infantry went in.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
The division had 1,100 men.
The division had 2,582 men. Each Guard cavalry regiment had squadrons in each of the three divisions; each division's are shown as one unit of each regiment.
Nafziger gives the division without brigades; its regiments are brigaded here as the list takes them.

forces.name: Friant's Old Guard
forces.summary: The Old Guard, marched from Soissons, which reached Reims at four in the afternoon and was held in reserve.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' Imperial Guard 1812 list, the nearest to 1814.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
The division had 3,800 men in eight battalions. The 1st Chasseurs and Grenadiers à Pied are the list's Old Guard, and the 2nd, raised in 1811, its Middle Guard.
Nafziger gives Michel as the commander of the chasseurs' brigade as well as of the 2nd Old Guard Division; the brigade is shown here without him.
Nafziger gives the Guard artillery together, seven foot and four horse batteries, not by division; the batteries here are those the list's brigades take.

forces.name: Boyer de Rébeval's Division
forces.summary: The division that had been Victor's, held in reserve with Friant's Old Guard.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1814: there is no list for the army Napoleon fought with in France, of the veterans of 1813, conscripts called up that winter and battalions drawn from depots across the Empire.

Nafziger has no order of battle for Reims. Marmont's infantry is from his VI Corps return of 12 March, the day before; Bordesoulle's cavalry from his return of the army on the Aisne of 17 March; and the Guard and Defrance's Gardes d'Honneur, which marched with Napoleon, from his returns for Craonne and Montmirail.
The division had 3,800 men in eleven battalions.

Nafziger gives these line battalions to Boyer de Rébeval as Victor's 9th Division, and Pierre Boyer a division of unknown battalions under Ney. Wikipedia's account has it the other way about: Pierre Boyer's 9th Division with Ney, and Boyer de Rébeval a provisional Young Guard division of conscripts with Victor. This follows Nafziger.
Its two foot batteries, eight 6-pdrs and four howitzers, are one in its divisional artillery and one in its reserve, as the list takes them.
Brigades of four regiments, where the list's take three, and two light regiments, where it allows one in the division, show as historical departures.

toCome.name: Exelmans's Division
toCome.summary: Advanced on Ricard's flanks with Colbert's, crossed the Vesle by the bridging train and led the pursuit; Nafziger doesn't identify its regiments.

toCome.name: Ney's Infantry
toCome.summary: Reached Reims before four in the afternoon; no return of it for March has been found.

toCome.name: Saint-Priest's Corps
toCome.formation: Gurgalov's 11th and Pillar's 17th Divisions, with Emmanuel's dragoons, VIII Infantry Corps
toCome.summary: About eight thousand men, who had taken Reims the day before. Saint-Priest was mortally wounded by a shell, and the corps fell back through the town in disorder.

toCome.name: Jagow's Brigade
toCome.summary: About five thousand men, surprised and broken at Gueux, Muizon and Thillois.
